preemption.details: New York does not have statewide preemption for knife laws. New York City, for example, enforces significantly stricter knife regulations than state law, including the (now-repealed) gravity knife enforcement under NYC Administrative Code.

open_carry.details: New York does not have a clear statewide rule on open carry of knives. Legality depends on the type of knife and local jurisdiction. Carrying a knife openly with intent to use unlawfully against another is a crime. NYC has additional restrictions.

statutes.title: Criminal possession of a weapon in the fourth degree

concealed_carry.details: Concealed carry depends on the type of knife and intent. It is illegal to possess certain dangerous knives (switchblades, gravity knives, pilum ballistic knives, cane swords, etc.) with intent to use unlawfully. Common pocketknives carried without unlawful intent are generally permitted.

statutes.title: Criminal possession of a weapon in the fourth degree

blade_length.details: New York does not impose a statewide blade length limit. However, NYC Administrative Code § 10-133 prohibits carrying a knife with a blade of 4 inches or longer in public.

switchblade.details: Switchblades (any knife with a blade that opens automatically by pressing a button, spring, or other device in the handle) are criminal to possess in the fourth degree under NY Penal Law § 265.01.

statutes.title: Criminal possession of a weapon — switchblade

automatic.details: Automatic knives are treated as switchblades under New York law and are therefore illegal to possess.

statutes.title: Criminal possession of a weapon — switchblade

assisted_opening.details: New York law does not specifically address assisted-opening knives. Whether an assisted-opening knife is classified as a switchblade depends on interpretation. Some legal opinions distinguish them from switchblades because manual force is required. Exercise caution.

ballistic_knife.details: Ballistic knives (referred to as 'pilum ballistic knives' in the statute) are specifically listed as illegal weapons under NY Penal Law.

restricted_locations.summary: Schools, government buildings, courts, airports. NYC has additional broad restrictions on knives in public.
restricted_locations.details: Possession of weapons (including certain knives) on school grounds is a felony under NY Penal Law § 265.01-a. NYC Administrative Code imposes additional restrictions on carrying knives in public view or with blades of 4 inches or more.

statutes.title: Criminal possession of a weapon on school grounds
